A federal appeals court struck down the 150-year-old ban on home distilling, ruling Congress can't use the tax power as a tool of prohibition. This is a win for hobbyists—and for the principle that federal power has constitutional limits.  

Learn more: ow.ly/mO3r50YK8bS

Under the Trump administration the number of refugees who enter legally and are granted full protection based on their fears of persecution has declined by nearly 90%, reports Cato’s @David_J_Bier. 

ow.ly/9x7H50YK2RB

Americans are angry about affordability, and policymakers face mounting pressure to “do something." 

Cato’s “Handbook on Affordability” offers 100+ practical policy ideas to improve monetary and fiscal policy — and lower prices by opening up supply and competition in food, energy, housing, healthcare, and more. 

ow.ly/gFJV50YKuqn

The Cato Institute welcomes Charles “Charlie” Sunderland to its Board of Directors.  
  
“We’re delighted that Charlie has joined Cato as a director, further strengthening our outstanding board,” said Peter Goettler, President and CEO of Cato. “He brings to the Institute an outstanding record of experience and success in business, a first-rate intellect, and full alignment with Cato’s principles and mission.” 

ow.ly/5EgC50YKvLs

High prices are squeezing Americans – and Washington's usual fixes would only make things worse. Cato's new Handbook on Affordability offers over 100 policy ideas to lower inflation and reduce core living costs, without the empty promises.

ow.ly/XUXi50YKuV4

What can life on the front lines of criminal justice teach us about American law today? Join @RandyEBarnett for a discussion of his new memoir, Felony Review: Tales of True Crime and Corruption in Chicago. nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1dKrPEwAP…

The new Economic Report of the President correctly identifies regulations as a real driver of housing costs but also misfires by ignoring Trump’s tariffs and pushing unsupported claims about immigrants and housing investors, explains Cato’s @sslivinski.

ow.ly/a8al50YK0Sp

When the FTC uses its power to punish a watchdog group for critical reporting, it threatens press freedom for everyone. Cato filed a legal brief arguing the First Amendment bars both direct retaliation and coercive government threats against speech.

ow.ly/3rII50YJYBl

The federal government can stop funding inmate gender transitions without blocking individuals from paying for their own care. Cato’s Matthew Cavedon argues the Trump administration should lift the restriction and allow inmates and supporters to fund these treatments themselves. 
Learn More: ow.ly/kuJF50YK1mg

Embracing free enterprise and innovation—that's how we fix the power grid and win the AI race, says Cato’s @ts_fisher. 

What makes America great is free enterprise. Let’s put it to work. 
 
Learn more: ow.ly/syCz50YImIH

Video

The only thing worse than getting robbed would be having the robber demand endless forms about the money he stole from you. Taxes are no different, says Cato’s @EconWithNick. 

ow.ly/UMBM50YK3uL

The Trump administration’s $100,000 fee has likely cut H-1B visas by at least 25%, Cato’s @David_J_Bier reports. 
 
Learn more: ow.ly/8BrV50YJ9IJ

The top 10% pays 60% of all federal taxes, the bottom 20% pays effectively nothing, and last year’s tax cuts added new complexity. In a new Cato Podcast episode, @CatoEdwards and @adamnmichel unpack the numbers and make the case for real reform. 
 
Apple: ow.ly/wMka50YK5aB   
Spotify: ow.ly/CBq350YK5aC  
Our website: ow.ly/9LP650YK5az

Congress votes on FISA 702 reauthorization today, yet the FBI delayed court-ordered release of its FISA noncompliance records—denying lawmakers and the public key oversight information about this sweeping surveillance power.

ow.ly/hqG850YK14w

Buying a cup of coffee with Bitcoin every day can result in over 100 pages of tax filings. That makes no sense. Cato’s @EconWithNick explains that capital gains rules turn everyday spending into a compliance nightmare. Congress can fix this. 

ow.ly/oSSb50YK3pz

Frustration over affordability is largely due to the post-pandemic inflation created in Washington, DC, through expansionary monetary and fiscal policy.

On April 16, we are releasing the Cato “Handbook on Affordability,” featuring 100+ policy ideas to defuse the risk of inflation’s re-emergence and to lower the cost of living.

President Trump reposted Cato’s immigration research. In this piece, our Director of Immigration Studies @David_J_Bier breaks down what the data actually show. 
  
“We do publish the facts, regardless of what they show, because that’s what intellectual honesty requires,” says Bier. 
  
ow.ly/NTqm50YK0qx

Health coverage does not equal health care. South Korea’s experience shows that government-designed health systems can promise universal access while leaving patients waiting when it matters most.
